z_cl.quote: This gives a plate scale of ~3.3 kpc/arcsec at the redshift (z=0.2) of Abell 520. All the quoted uncertainties are at the 1-sigma (~68%) level.

I.type: P4 (weak-lensing mass substructure centroid, ACS maximum-entropy/FIATMAP mass reconstruction; centroid from Gaussian-weighted first moments)
I.location: Table 1 'Mass Properties of Substructure (r<150 kpc)', row P4; centroid method in §4.1 'Centroid and Significance of the Dark Peak in A520'

uncertainty.location: Table 1 column header 'Δα, Δδ (″,″)' and table comment; confidence level from §1 general statement
uncertainty.quote: Table 1 header: \colhead{$\Delta \alpha, \Delta \delta$} ... \colhead{ ($\arcsec,\arcsec$)}; tablecomments: 'The positional uncertainty is estimated from bootstrapping.'; §4.1: 'We measure the centroids using the first moments weighted by a circular Gaussian, whose FWHM matches the size of the substructure. The results are displayed in Table~1. The mean positional uncertainty is small (~5″)'; §1: 'All the quoted uncertainties are at the 1-sigma (~68%) level.'

G.type: X-ray peak / gas core of P4 subcluster
G.quote: No X-ray position for P4 is given. Only qualitative X-ray statements concern the dark peak P3': '…its position has shifted … and now coincides well with the peak in the X-ray emission' (§7); and '…the location of the bow-shock feature indicates that P4 may correspond to the "bullet" of the Bullet Cluster' (§7). Table 1 'Gas Mass' column for P4 is an upper limit '<0.34', not a position.

notes: Only x_I (P4) with per-axis bootstrap errors (3.0, 4.4) arcsec is available. Neither an X-ray peak position nor any galaxy/BCG/luminosity-centroid position for P4 is given anywhere in the paper (searched full LaTeX for coordinates '04 54', 'X-ray', 'BCG', 'brightest', 'centroid', 'luminosity'); no numerical I-G or I-S offset for P4 is stated. Pointer mismatch: in the arXiv source, Table 1 is in §4 (Mass reconstruction); §3.2 is 'PSF Model' and contains no positions. Other Table 1 rows for context: P3' (new dark-peak centroid) (04 54 07.51, +02 54 41.3) (5.1,6.2). Interpretation note: 'Δα' is given in arcsec (header), i.e. presumably an on-sky arcsec error, not seconds of RA.
